body:
Alright, I think I found something. We are using a multi-module maven project, where we have a dedicated database module with Quarkus dependencies, but it doesn't include any RESTeasy dependencies. Once I add `quarkus-resteasy` to that module the integration tests pass again.

Provided a minimal reproducer here https://github.com/wjglerum/quarkus-panache

Good catch. The issue is that the new `QuarkusConnectionCache` in Agroal has a hard dependency to Netty... and it compiles because the optional `quarkus-smallrye-health` brings Netty into the compile classpath of the extension.

We have two options here:
- either have Agroal dependent on Netty - not sure it's a good idea,
- or only use this cache if Netty is around.

@stuartwdouglas I can do the ground work but I would appreciate your opinion on what is best.

Optional dependencies strike again.

Is it even possible to run a Quarkus app w/o Netty nowadays?  If it's not possible we should just add the hard dependency.

rename.from: Integration tests are failing after Quarkus 2.1.1 update
rename.to: Agroal has a reference to a Netty class while not depending on it

body: looking into `quarkus-smallrye-health` dependency tree we pull netty through `io.quarkus:quarkus-vertx-http`,`io.quarkus:quarkus-arc-deployment`, and `io.quarkus:quarkus-vertx-http-deployment:`. Should I try to investigate if we can exclude netty? Do other extensions exclude it from these dependencies?

hi @xstefank ! AFAIK (but would like to hear confirmations from others) we almost always require Netty - perhaps only with CLI apps is it not required but I'm not sure. I'd suggest to get an authoritative answer about that first (Stuart will likely comment when he's back), so to not do such work without need.

issue.title: Fall back to ThreadLocal if Netty is not present

body: It is definitely possible to run without Netty, e.g. a CLI hibernate app. That said most extensions that do anything with the network rely on it.
